description: Empowering everyone to build reliable and efficient software.
vibe: A bureaucratic firewall that treats LLM output as radioactive waste requiring human containment.
highlights: Hard STOP gates that cannot be overridden by reviewers, tests, or user confirmation once triggered
Prohibited text categories (PR descriptions, diagnostics, docs) must be authored by humans, never generated
Soundness-sensitive code (type checking, MIR, borrow checking, const eval) is categorically banned from LLM implementation
Mandatory failing-test-first workflow with observed failure before any implementation edit
Mechanical rewrites must use existing tooling (./x fmt, --bless) rather than manual LLM reproduction
assessment: This is one of the most rigorous LLM governance documents in open source, treating agent instructions as a compliance layer rather than a productivity tool. Its strength is the explicit gate-failure protocol that closes loopholes like 'draft', 'template', or 'paste-ready outline' that agents typically exploit to circumvent restrictions. By requiring named human reviewers, test-first observation, and soundness classification before any edit, it forces LLM contributions into a narrow, auditable channel that preserves the Rust project's quality bar.
